key_insight: AI-generated synthetic clinical data can closely mirror real dyslipidemia datasets and preserve key research signals for secondary cardiovascular prevention.
clinical_relevance: This suggests synthetic data may help researchers analyze and model cardiovascular risk and lipid-treatment outcomes when access to real patient data is restricted.
method: Fine-tuned pre-trained large language models on two real-world Centro Cardiologico Monzino clinical datasets.
Generated synthetic tabular records within a secure infrastructure to preserve data sovereignty.
Compared synthetic vs. real data using fidelity, privacy, and downstream modeling performance metrics.
evidence_signal: Synthetic data outperformed classic anonymization in the abstract, with strong real-vs-synthetic agreement and preserved predictors such as therapy modification, creatine phosphokinase, and pharmacological intensity.
watch_item: Some effect sizes were slightly attenuated, so synthetic data should be validated before use in high-stakes or confirmatory analyses.
paper_title: Evaluation of AI-Generated Synthetic Data for Clinical Research in Secondary Cardiovascular Prevention among Dyslipidemia Patients
